title: 4 months ago I started building the mmorpg I've dreamed of since I was a kid.
author: ImeldaOnline_
selftext:
Ever since I played the old-school grind MMOs, I've wanted to make my own. Huge packs of monsters, loot that changes how your character looks, upgrading your armor, start a guild with your friends. But an MMORPG is a studio's work: code, servers, art, 3D models, animation, sound. For me, it was always a "maybe one day" dream.

**How I work**

**Code:** I build it together with Claude Code. I describe what I want and how it should feel, it writes and fixes the code, and I test everything. The game runs in the browser in plain JavaScript, with a multiplayer server behind it.

**Art:** image models running locally in ComfyUI on my own PC, with a LoRA trained on my own approved designs, so heroes, monsters and gear all feel like one world.

**3D:** approved designs go through image-to-3D, get rigged and animated, and are rendered into the game.

**Where it stands**

5 classes, dungeons and bosses, armor sets, upgrades, player stalls, mounts, parties, guilds, PvP and a weekly guild war. Four months ago none of it existed.

I'm not posting this to advertise. I wanted to share that a dream project like this is actually possible now for one person. Happy to answer anything about the workflow, the tools or what went wrong along the way.

comments.author: Foreign_Pitch_12
comments.body: What was the best way to connect art and code together? Did you feed the assets to claude manually via drive inbox or github? Or are all tools connected in Claude?

replies.author: ImeldaOnline_
replies.body: Hi, every tool is connected to Claude. Using ComfyUI I create assets/art and let Claude control it and I create the prompts.

replies.author: Foreign_Pitch_12
replies.body: Thank you for the answer. I will check comfyUI for my games UI.
